# InvoiceUI agent instructions

Follow these rules for this project. Read relevant detailed topics below only when needed; do not load every agent adapter.


# Project scope and precedence

- Build Humza's private invoice workspace: create invoices simply, access anywhere, download reliable PDFs. Preserve the existing editor/live-preview layout.
- Latest explicit user instructions take precedence over project preferences. IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md is the feature specification; CURSOR_PROMPTS.md breaks it into phases. Read only the relevant section. Verify CURSOR_PROGRESS.md claims against code when needed.
- Keep React/Vite/TypeScript, Tailwind, Hono, Neon, Resend and one Cloudflare Worker serving assets and API. Default GBP and Europe/London; tax is opt-in. Preserve established integrations unless the task needs a change.
- The mandatory UI stack is shadcn/ui, Motion (motion.dev), Animate UI, Magic UI and React Bits. Read 02 for all interface work.
- Work inside InvoiceUI. Sibling client folders contain historical material: do not scan/import/change them without a relevant user request.
- Card collection, automatic FX conversion and historical invoice import are future scope. Do not add them speculatively.


# Efficient work and agent handoffs

- Inspect current changes before editing; other agents may be active. Own a bounded set of files and preserve unrelated changes. Do not reset, clean, overwrite, stage or commit another agent's work.
- Read targeted source with rg; avoid dependencies, generated output and secret files. Consult .cursorignore. Do not reread all rules or the full plan each turn.
- Reuse current implementations and installed dependencies. Avoid sweeping refactors, speculative abstractions, repeated installs and duplicate test runs without changed evidence.
- Proceed on routine reversible decisions. Ask only for information genuinely needed; keep independent work moving. Do not create additional agents unless requested.
- Update the existing CURSOR_PROGRESS.md concisely at milestones; preserve others' entries. Record scope, decisions, checks, blockers and next action. Do not use it as a lock or claim completion without evidence.
- For concurrent work, coordinate overlapping edits; prefer separate worktrees when practical. Never terminate another agent's processes.
- Report outcomes briefly. Read required detailed rules once per task, not each tool call.


# Required UI libraries and provenance

- HARD USER REQUIREMENT: use all five libraries across the finished product: shadcn/ui, Motion from motion.dev, Animate UI (the requested Animated/Animation UI), Magic UI and React Bits. Do not quietly substitute hand-built lookalikes.
- Use shadcn/ui as the default for buttons, inputs, dialogs, selects, menus, sheets, tabs, toasts and other applicable accessible controls. Extend existing components and tokens before introducing new primitives.
- Use Motion for appropriate transitions and interaction feedback. Use real Animate UI, Magic UI and React Bits components for purposeful enhancements; all three must have actual rendered product usage before UI completion.
- This is a product-wide requirement, not a demand to import every library into every screen. Avoid five competing versions of the same control.
- Use official registries/source, verify API and licence, copy only selected components where appropriate, and preserve required attribution. Never invent registry commands or claim provenance for a homemade component.
- Maintain docs/UI_COMPONENT_SOURCES.md when adding vendor-derived components: library, component, source URL, licence, local path and screen where used. Record gaps honestly until implemented.
- Match the existing invoice workflow and design tokens. Respect reduced motion, keyboard access and performance. Keep animated decoration out of printed/PDF invoices.
- A dependency, unused import, library-name comment or provenance entry alone does not satisfy usage. Verify rendered behavior and include library coverage in UI handoffs.


# Shared rules ignore policy and maintenance

- Canonical numbered rules live in .cursor/rules, project skills in .cursor/skills, and shared ignores in .cursorignore. Other agent adapters are generated by `npm run sync:agents`; edit the Cursor files then run that command. Use `npm run sync:agents:check` to detect drift.
- Two-digit prefixes organise topics, not precedence. Latest explicit user instructions override project preferences. The five-library UI requirement is deliberate; ordinary guidance supports practical judgment.
- Read 00, 01, 02, 11 and 12 at task start; read other topics only when relevant. If already supplied by the agent, do not reread the same text.
- .cursorignore is the portable context exclusion source. .cursorindexingignore is Cursor-only indexing noise and is not copied to other agents. Native ignore support varies; never claim these files create a universal security sandbox.
- Keep source, tests, migrations, manifests, lockfiles, environment examples, rule files and design assets available. Ignore secrets, dependency trees, caches, runtime state, logs, database dumps and private exports.
- Do not bypass access restrictions through a terminal or script. For a relevant ignored synthetic artifact, narrow its policy only when authorised; do not remove secret exclusions to make a task easier.
- Keep compatibility notes in .ai/README.md current. Do not create fictional native ignore/config filenames or change global permissions, models or user settings.


# Punctuation: regular dashes only

- HARD USER REQUIREMENT: never use an em dash (Unicode U+2014) in agent-authored text. That includes replies, comments, commits, GitHub markdown, rules, docs, changelogs, UI copy you write, and generated files.
- Use a regular ASCII hyphen-minus (-) instead. For asides, use commas, parentheses, a colon, or a spaced hyphen: `word - word`.
- Do not use an en dash (Unicode U+2013) either. Ranges are `1-5` or `phases 1-5`, not typographic dashes.
- When you edit a file, replace em dashes and en dashes in the text you touch. Do not add new ones. Leave third-party or generated vendor files unchanged.
- Do not sneak the character in via HTML entities (`&mdash;`, `&#8212;`) or copy-paste from models that prefer em dashes.


# Fluid motion, tactile feedback, and interactive animations

- HARD USER REQUIREMENT: all interactive elements must feel fluid, reactive, and physically responsive to mouse hovers, focus, and clicks. Nothing in the interface should feel instant, stiff, or abrupt.
- Apply tailored cubic-bezier easing curves (such as `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) across interactive element transitions: background-color, border-color, box-shadow, and transform.
- Interactive controls (buttons, chips, cards, list rows, badges, inputs) must provide clear tactile feedback: subtle hover lift and soft elevation glow on hover, followed by a slight physical depression or scale down (e.g. `scale(0.98)`) on `:active:not(:disabled)`.
- Modals, sheets, tooltips, command dialogs, and floating bulk action bars must enter and exit smoothly with spring scale and backdrop fade rather than snapping into view instantly.
- Contextual actions, toolbar triggers, and state feedback must incorporate animated Lucide icons from Animate UI (located in `src/client/components/ui/AnimatedIcon.tsx`), including Search, Refresh, Plus, Download, ExternalLink, Arrow navigation, Check, Copy, Trash, and X close.
- HARD USER REQUIREMENT: save and form commit buttons across the workspace must use the interactive state-switching button effect (`StateButton`, derived from Magic UI Animated Subscribe Button, Motion spring transitions, and Animate UI animated icons): smoothly morphing from idle state through an active saving state with tactile spinner feedback to a confirmed saved state before completing or settling.
- Animated icons should activate cleanly on hover (`animateOnHover`) or tap, enhancing clarity without interrupting user tasks or workflow rhythm.
- Respect reduced motion accessibility unconditionally: honor `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and Motion's `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">`.
- Animated decoration must never leak into printed or generated PDF documents. Enforce clean document layouts under `@media print` and inside PDF generation pipelines.


# No browser alerts: only UI modals

- HARD USER REQUIREMENT: never use browser-native `alert()`, `confirm()`, or `prompt()` anywhere in the codebase.
- All user alerts, confirmations, notices, and destructive action prompts must be presented using proper UI-created modals built with shadcn/ui and Radix Dialog primitives (via the project `useConfirm` hook or `Modal` components).
- Confirmation modals must provide a clear, descriptive title, contextual body explanation, and distinct action buttons (e.g. secondary "Cancel" and danger or primary confirmation).
- Every modal must adhere to the design system: backdrop blur, spring scale transitions, tactile button press feedback (`scale(0.98)` on active), accessible keyboard focus traps, and Escape key dismissal.
- Alert and notice messages must feel integrated with the application rather than interrupting the user with native browser popups.
